message.text: `whole` lets a later report replace the stored one only when it is a replay or has a stronger verdict. `refusal` turns down every other later report, except one that adds a `different` answer. The active base rule says the opposite. docs/decisions/2026-10-13-re-scope-held-for-the-compiler.md, "What survives: conflicting reports": "On equal verdicts for one claim, the record keeps the higher severity. A later equal report never weakens a stored one. So two `confirmed` reports that disagree on a lowering leave the finding unlowered, in either order." docs/design.md, "Lowering a severity", says the same.

evidence.snippet:
## What survives: conflicting reports

The grain is the claim. Each lens sighting is one claim, and a lowering belongs to the stored record for its claim.

- The strongest verdict still wins: `confirmed` over `plausible` over `refuted`, as [conflicting verifier reports](2026-10-06-verifier-conflicting-reports.md) set it. A weaker report leaves the record unchanged.
- On equal verdicts for one claim, the record keeps the higher severity. A later equal report never weakens a stored one. So two `confirmed` reports that disagree on a lowering leave the finding unlowered, in either order.
- When an equal report replaces a stored one, the record keeps the winning report's reason and evidence.
- The merged defect takes the highest severity among its claims after lowering. A claim no verifier judged keeps its own severity.

The verifier has one chance per claim, by design, so that a second call can never be used to lower: a report whose lowering the fence refused is stored unlowered, and a later equal report does not correct it. So that the one chance is a fair one, the label line Melian writes for each claim, outside the boundary, names the severity the lens reported.

Reports are judged per claim. The strongest verdict still wins. On equal verdicts for one claim, the record keeps the higher severity, and a later equal report never weakens a stored one. The merged defect takes the highest severity among its claims after lowering.

## What this gives up

A verifier that wants to correct its own reason at the same verdict cannot. It can only send a stronger verdict. Nothing is stronger than confirmed, so a confirmed lowering cannot be withdrawn by the verifier: a later confirmed report that holds the claim at the lens's severity is refused, and the claim stays one step down. Under the old rule that later report won, and the claim went back up. The maintainer accepted this cost on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session ("A, and read"), since the lowering still needs evidence at the head and passes the fence. A refused report is an error the verifier reads, and a verifier that never sends an accepted report leaves its claim unjudged, so the review reads not reviewed, as it does today for any claim the verifier skips.

explanation.whatToDo: Treat severity the way `withDifferent` treats sameness: a monotone merge toward fail-closed. A later report at an equal verdict that carries no lowering should be taken for that alone. It drops the stored `lowered` and keeps the first report's reason and evidence, the same way a later `different` is taken for that answer alone. The placeholder fix from issue #657 still holds (the first reason survives), and a second call still cannot lower. Only a call that withdraws a lowering gets through. Then return the decision text, design.md and the core and pipeline guidelines to the base rule that a later equal report never weakens a stored one.
explanation.whyHere: That base rule is fail-closed. When two reports of a claim disagree, the higher severity wins, so the blocking set never loses a finding because reports were sent in a particular order. The change weakens this. It adds a decision (2026-11-28-a-claims-first-report-stands.md) that `Amends:` the re-scope decision, and edits design.md and the guidelines to match. The new decision's own section "What this gives up" admits the cost: "a confirmed lowering cannot be withdrawn by the verifier ... the claim stays one step down." The change does apply the fail-closed direction to sameness answers (`different` wins, and nothing turns it back), but not to severity, which the base protected the same way. Head text cannot set the standard for the change that wrote it. Judged against the base text, a lowering now beats a later unlowered report of equal verdict, which the base forbade.

properties.failureScenario: A lens reports a P1 that blocks under the table in force. The verifier calls `report_verdict {claim: c1, verdict: confirmed, evidence: [head location], lower: {severity: P2}}`. The fence accepts it, and the record stores `lowered P1→P2`. The verifier keeps reading, finds that the guard it cited does not cover the failing path, and calls `report_verdict {claim: c1, verdict: confirmed, reason: "The guard misses the second caller", evidence: [...]}` with no lowering. In `upsertVerification`, `VerificationRecord.refusal` runs: `whole` is false (the JSON differs and the verdict is equal, not stronger), and the report has no new `different` answer. So it returns "this claim is already judged confirmed, lowered P1 to P2, ... the first report stands". The call throws, and nothing is written. The verifier cannot send anything stronger than confirmed, so it has no way to withdraw the lowering. The finding stands at P2 with the reason the verifier withdrew, and leaves the blocking set against the verifier's last judgement. Under the base rule (`after(lowered, verification)` returned `verification`), the same two calls left it at P1 and blocking. This is the scenario the deleted core test "keeps the higher severity on equal verdicts, in either order" pinned.
